cards.text: Hosea the prophet is still bringing the LORD's message about Ephraim, Israel's northern kingdom, called by the name of its leading tribe (Hosea 11:8). Once upon a time, when Ephraim spoke, people TREMBLED. He was exalted in Israel, the one who talked and the whole room went quiet.

cards.question: Ephraim was exalted in Israel. But then he incurred guilt, and he died. What did Ephraim incur guilt through?

cards.text: And it doesn't stop there. Now they sin more and more, turning their own silver into cast images, idols skillfully made by craftsmen. FIVE-STAR craftsmanship. Zero-star idea.

cards.question: Hosea says people have a saying about all this idol making. True or false: the saying talks about kissing the calves.

cards.text: The full saying is even darker: "They offer human sacrifice and kiss the calves!" So where does chasing idols get them? Next come four quick pictures of what they'll be like.

cards.question: They'll be like the morning mist, like early dew, like chaff blown from a threshing floor, and like smoke through an open window. What do all four pictures have in common?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks: "Yet I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt; you know no God but Me, for there is no Savior besides Me."

cards.question: The LORD goes way back with His people, all the way to Egypt. He says He knew them in the ___, in the land of drought.

cards.text: Then they finally get pasture, and when they have pasture, they're satisfied. Full, comfy, feet up.

cards.question: Once the people are satisfied in their pasture, their hearts become proud. What happens as a result?

cards.text: Pray hard for the job, get the job, and the praying stops on payday. Here, the LORD answers with wild animals: He'll be like a lion pouncing, like a leopard lurking by the path, like a wild beast tearing them apart.

cards.question: One more animal joins the lion and the leopard. The LORD says He will attack them like a ___ robbed of her cubs.

cards.text: After all those wild animals, the LORD drops the pictures and talks straight to Israel. No pictures this time. Just the truth, and it lands harder than a rolling pin off the top shelf.

cards.question: The LORD tells Israel they are destroyed. Why does He say it happened?

answers.text: Their king lost a great battle

cards.text: Then the LORD asks where their king is now to save them, and the rulers they asked for, a king and princes. It's like hiring the guy who swore he'd fix everything, and the night the storm hits, he's not picking up.

cards.question: The LORD talks about the king Israel asked for. True or false: the LORD says He gave Israel a king as a reward.

cards.text: In His anger He gave them a king, and in His wrath He took him away. And Ephraim's sin is bound up and stored up, the one box in the whole bakery I would NEVER want to open.

cards.question: Ephraim is pictured as a baby about to be born. Labor pains come upon him, but he is an unwise son. When the time arrives, what happens?

answers.text: He fails to present himself at the womb
He is born into a king's house
He is born holding his brother's heel

cards.text: Then, right in the middle of all this, the LORD calls out, "Where, O Death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your sting?"

cards.question: Just before the LORD calls out to Death and Sheol, what does He say He will do for His people?

cards.text: But the verse ends, "Compassion is hidden from My eyes." Ephraim may be flourishing among his brothers, but a wind is coming.

cards.question: The east wind coming against Ephraim is a wind from ___.
True or false: when the east wind comes, Ephraim's spring keeps on flowing.

cards.text: His fountain fails, his spring runs dry, and the wind plunders his treasury of every precious article. Then the message turns to Samaria, a city of Israel (1 Kings 16:24).

cards.question: Samaria will bear her guilt. Why?

cards.text: And the cost is terrible. They will fall by the sword, and even the little ones and the pregnant women will not be spared.
